item.text:
I completed targeted internet research, but could not persist changes: the workspace is read-only and local commands were blocked by the sandbox. No notebook or `research-ledger-manifest.json` update was written.

Recovered source-claim units for manual insertion:

- `GH-2000-4B-01` — IPU, *Ghana parliamentary elections 2000*, election narrative: Rawlings stepped down under the constitutional two-term limit; the Osu Declaration committed candidates to nonviolent campaigns; OAU observers declared voting/counting transparent; Bawku violence killed at least 13. Period fit: exact 2000. Attribution: Rawlings’s constitutional exit and campaign environment, not responsibility for all violence. Links 4B.1–4B.3, 4B.8–4B.9. Contrary evidence: Bawku deaths and rival-party clashes. [IPU election record](https://archive.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/arc/2123_00.htm)

- `GH-2000-5B-01` — Ghana Ministry of Finance, *2000 Budget Statement*, official repository landing page. It establishes a contemporaneous Rawlings-government budget document, but the HTML page does not expose the PDF text. Disposition: `context_pending_pdf_locator`; do not treat as final until PDF page/section locators are extracted. [Ministry of Finance](https://www.mofep.gov.gh/budget-statements/2000)

- `GH-2000-5B-02` — IMF, *Letter of Intent and Memorandum of Economic and Financial Policies*, 25 June 2000, paragraphs 1–3 and 14–16: the government set 2000–02 poverty-reduction objectives, adjusted policy after the cocoa/gold/oil shock, targeted at least 4% growth in 2000, protected health and education spending, and aimed toward fiscal balance. Exact period fit; ruler attribution is to the government under Rawlings, not personal authorship. Links 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.6–5B.8, 8B.1–8B.7. Contrary evidence: implementation delays and the severe external shock. [IMF memorandum](https://www.imf.org/external/np/loi/2000/gha/01/index.htm)

- `GH-2000-5B-03` — Same IMF memorandum, paragraphs 10–11: banking-sector closures, draft banking laws submitted to Parliament in May 2000, Tema Oil Refinery restructuring, and planned divestitures. Exact period fit and concrete execution evidence. Attribution: government policy implementation; avoid converting it into a personal Rawlings claim. Links 5B.7, 8B.2, 8B.6–8B.8. Contrary evidence: delayed Ghana Railways transaction and halted Ghana Airways divestiture. [IMF memorandum](https://www.imf.org/external/np/loi/2000/gha/01/index.htm)

- `GH-2000-7B-01` — Same IMF memorandum, paragraph 13: the Serious Fraud Office investigated 37 alleged fraud, embezzlement, tax-evasion, and misappropriation cases involving 9.5 billion cedis and recovered about 2.2 billion; the government invited World Bank cooperation on corruption perceptions. Exact period fit. Attribution: institutional anti-corruption action under Rawlings’s government, not proof of personal integrity. Links 7B.5–7B.7. Contrary evidence: the text reports allegations and investigations, not convictions. [IMF memorandum](https://www.imf.org/external/np/loi/2000/gha/01/index.htm)

- `GH-2000-8B-01` — Same IMF memorandum, paragraphs 17–18 and 33–36: cocoa-market reforms, planned divestitures, monthly monitoring, September/October review, and corrective-action mechanisms. Exact period fit. Attribution: government coordination and monitoring structures. Links 8B.1–8B.8. Contrary evidence: several targets were prospective, and the document records delayed implementation. [IMF memorandum](https://www.imf.org/external/np/loi/2000/gha/01/index.htm)

- `GH-2000-3B-01` — U.S. State Department, *Country Report on Human Rights Practices 2000—Ghana*, sections 1.c and 2.a, especially paragraphs corresponding to the 64th Infantry Regiment case and press restrictions: an alleged two-week detention and abuse case remained under investigation; military authorities acknowledged detention but denied abuse; officials warned against using soldiers for private disputes; two journalists remained under sedition prosecution; a journalist was detained on 13 January and another on 5 January. Exact period fit. Attribution: documented state/security conduct and government response, not proof Rawlings personally ordered each act. Links 3B.1–3B.5, 3B.8–3B.10; 7B.1 and 7B.7. Contrary evidence: official denials and announced investigations. [State Department report](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/usdos/2001/en/25747)

- `GH-2000-3B-02` — CPJ, 7 February 2000 letter to President Rawlings, paragraphs beginning “Blay-Amihere was first arrested” and “On February 3”: soldiers detained and interrogated editor Kabral Blay-Amihere over an editorial; the army required a prepared apology; police investigated possible sedition carrying a minimum five-year sentence. Exact period fit and direct ruler-addressed attribution. Links 3B.1, 3B.5, 3B.8 and 7B.1, 7B.7. Contrary evidence: CPJ is reporting the incident and requesting intervention, not adjudicating Rawlings’s personal order. [CPJ letter](https://cpj.org/2000/02/ghana-editor-threatened-with-sedition-charges/)

- `GH-2000-4B-02` — African Commission, Ghana’s second periodic report covering 1993–2000, conclusion: it reports a “commendable rise” in parliamentary democracy and liberalism and overall improvement in rights after the 1992 Constitution and CHRAJ’s creation, while noting continuing barriers to effective rights enjoyment. Period fit: cumulative through 2000. Attribution: institutional trajectory under Rawlings, not a personal decision. Links 3B.4, 4B.2, 4B.8, 7B.6. Contrary evidence: inadequate rights education, funding, and adverse cultural norms. [ACHPR report](https://achpr.au.int/en/state-reports/ghana-2nd-periodic-report-1993-2000)

- `GH-2000-1B-01` — IAEA Office of Legal Affairs, Ghana country factsheet: Ghana’s NPT safeguards agreement entered into force in 1975; the Additional Protocol was signed in 1998 and entered into force in 2004. Use only as treaty/status context, not ruler conduct. Links 1B.1, 1B.4, 1B.6, 1B.10. [IAEA Ghana factsheet](https://ola.iaea.org/Applications/FactSheets/Country/Detail?code=GH)
